title: Assembly & BOM Review
description: Checks that the BOM, footprints, placement data, stencil, soldering process and assembly documentation let an assembler build the board right first time.

items.text: BOM is exported from the schematic at the release revision, with no manual edits
items.hint: Hand-edited BOMs drift from the design. Regenerate from the CAD tool and diff against the previous release BOM.

items.text: Every component has a manufacturer part number (MPN) assigned
items.hint: Without an MPN the assembler picks a part for you. Generic values like "10k 0402" are not enough for a build.

items.text: Every line has at least one approved distributor with stock and lead time checked
items.hint: Check at the build quantity, not just a single unit. Record the date the check was made.

items.text: Alternate or equivalent parts are listed where applicable
items.hint: Confirm each alternate is a true form-fit-function match: footprint, pinout, voltage rating, tolerance and temperature range.

items.text: No obsolete, NRND or EOL parts are used without an approved substitute
items.hint: Check lifecycle status at the manufacturer or a distributor shortly before release; status changes without notice.

items.text: Per-board quantities match the reference designator count, with DNP items clearly flagged
items.hint: Use a dedicated DNP field rather than notes in the description, so the assembler's import picks it up.

items.text: BOM reference designators match the schematic exactly
items.hint: Look for missing, duplicated or renamed refdes after back-annotation.

items.text: Every line has a complete description: value, tolerance, rating, dielectric and package
items.hint: "10 µF 0805" is ambiguous: X7R vs Y5V and the voltage rating change the effective capacitance under DC bias.

items.text: The package of every MPN matches the footprint used on the PCB
items.hint: An 0402 part ordered for an 0603 footprint, or a QFN ordering code for an SOIC footprint, stops the build.

items.text: Each build variant has its own BOM, identified by an assembly part number
items.hint: Variants managed by memory get built wrong. Make the variant visible on the BOM, the assembly drawing and ideally the board label.

items.text: Single-source parts are identified and the supply risk accepted
items.hint: Flag them for the project lead; consider a second-source footprint or a buffer stock for critical ones.

items.text: Long-lead parts are identified and ordered or reserved early
items.hint: Treat anything well beyond typical distributor lead time (rule of thumb: over ~12 weeks) as a schedule risk.

items.text: Consigned (customer-supplied) and turnkey parts are identified line by line
items.hint: Assemblers need to know which parts they buy and which arrive in a kit, or lines end up short or double-bought.

items.text: Mechanical items (fasteners, standoffs, heatsinks, shields, labels) are on the BOM
items.hint: Non-electrical parts are often missing because they have no schematic symbol. Add them as BOM-only items.

items.text: Programmable parts are identified with the firmware image and version to load
items.hint: Say whether the assembler programs them pre-placement, in-circuit, or if programming happens at test.

items.text: Parts in automotive builds are AEC-Q qualified where required
items.hint: Check the exact ordering code: the AEC-Q grade is often a suffix, and the standard part is not qualified.

items.text: Every footprint is verified against the manufacturer's datasheet land pattern
items.hint: Check pad size, pitch, body outline and any exposed pad. Library parts copied from other projects are a common source of error.

items.text: Component heights are checked against mechanical constraints (lid, heatsink, mating boards)
items.hint: Use 3D models or the max-height dimension from the datasheet, not the typical value.

items.text: SMD and through-hole components are clearly distinguished in the BOM and assembly drawing
items.hint: The assembler routes each to a different process; mixing them up adds cost and delay.

items.text: Polarized components (diodes, electrolytics, ICs) have their orientation marked
items.hint: Mark polarity on silkscreen and the assembly drawing so it is still visible after the part is placed.

items.text: Fine-pitch and BGA components are reviewed for reflow profile compatibility
items.hint: Large BGAs and small passives on the same board may need a compromise profile; check with the assembler.

items.text: Land patterns follow IPC-7351 with the density level (most, nominal, least) chosen deliberately
items.hint: Nominal suits most reflow builds; least for very dense boards; most for hand soldering or wave.

items.text: Pin 1 is marked on silkscreen and the assembly layer, outside the part body
items.hint: A pin-1 dot hidden under the body cannot be checked after placement.

items.text: Footprint pad numbers match the schematic symbol pin numbers for every unique part
items.hint: Watch SOT-23 transistors and regulators (pinouts vary by vendor), connectors and mirrored headers.

items.text: The footprint matches the exact package variant of the ordered MPN
items.hint: One IC often comes in QFN, DFN and WSON variants with different pad sizes or exposed pads. Check the ordering code.

items.text: Thermal vias in exposed pads are tented, plugged or filled to stop solder wicking
items.hint: Open vias drain solder away from the joint and cause voids or a lifted part. Agree the treatment with fab and assembler.

items.text: Connector footprints include mechanical retention features (hold-down pads, bosses, pegs)
items.hint: Surface-mount connectors without anchoring tear off under cable load.

items.text: BGA pads are mask-defined or copper-defined as the package datasheet recommends
items.hint: Mixing the two on one package gives uneven joints.

items.text: Fine-pitch pads have solder mask dams between them, where fab capability allows
items.hint: Without a dam, bridges are more likely. If the web is below fab minimum, agree a gang relief instead.

items.text: No open vias are placed in SMD pads unless filled and capped
items.hint: Open via-in-pad wicks solder and gives voids or starved joints.

items.text: Small passives have balanced copper connections on both pads
items.hint: One pad on a plane and the other on a thin trace heats unevenly and tombstones. Use thermal relief on plane connections.

items.text: Centroid file lists refdes, X, Y, rotation and side for every placed part
items.hint: Generate it from the release PCB file, not an earlier one.

items.text: DNP parts are handled in the centroid file the same way as in the BOM
items.hint: Either remove DNP parts or flag them; a mismatch between BOM and centroid causes placement of parts meant to be left off.

items.text: Centroid file units and origin are stated and match the board origin on the drawing
items.hint: Use mm and a board origin at a defined corner or datum, not an arbitrary CAD origin.

items.text: The rotation convention is confirmed with the assembler
items.hint: CAD library zero orientation often differs from the IPC-7351 convention. Ask for a first-article check of rotations.

items.text: Each part's placement origin is at the body center
items.hint: Footprints with the origin at pin 1 or a corner give offset placements unless the assembler corrects them.

items.text: The bottom-side coordinate convention (mirrored or viewed from top) is stated
items.hint: Bottom-side X and rotation are frequently misinterpreted; say which view the numbers are in.

items.text: The board (or panel) has at least three global fiducials, not in a straight line
items.hint: Rule of thumb; follow the assembler's preferred fiducial size and position.

items.text: Local fiducials are placed near fine-pitch and BGA parts where the assembler asks for them
items.hint: Local fiducials correct for board stretch around critical parts.

items.text: Components keep clear of board edges used for conveyor rails, or a panel rail is added
items.hint: Clearance needed depends on the assembler's line; ask before layout is frozen.

items.text: The paste layer has apertures on every pad to be soldered and none on pads that must stay bare
items.hint: Remove paste from test points, fiducials, edge fingers and hand-solder pads.

items.text: Stencil thickness is agreed with the assembler for the finest-pitch part
items.hint: Common rule of thumb is 0.10–0.13 mm (4–5 mil); the assembler will confirm for your part mix.

items.text: Aperture area ratio is acceptable for the smallest apertures
items.hint: Rule of thumb: an area ratio of about 0.66 or more for reliable release. Check with the stencil supplier for 0201 and fine-pitch BGA.

items.text: Exposed-pad apertures are split into a windowpane pattern to limit paste coverage
items.hint: Follow the package datasheet; too much paste floats the part and opens the perimeter joints.

items.text: Paste reductions on fine-pitch and BGA pads follow the assembler's recommendation
items.hint: Many assemblers apply their own aperture rules; state whether yours or theirs take priority.

items.text: Parts needing extra paste (large connectors, shields) are covered by a step stencil or overprint
items.hint: A single thickness rarely suits both 0.4 mm pitch parts and large connector tabs.

items.text: Solder paste type is specified: alloy, powder type and flux chemistry
items.hint: No-clean vs water-soluble flux affects cleaning and coating. Finer powder types suit finer pitch.

items.text: Every part's peak temperature and time-above-liquidus limits suit the planned reflow profile
items.hint: Check connectors, crystals, electrolytics, LEDs and plastic switches, which often have lower limits than ICs.

items.text: The assembler's dry storage and bake handling is confirmed for MSL 3 and higher parts
items.hint: Parts out of the bag beyond floor life crack or delaminate in reflow (popcorning).

items.text: Bottom-side parts are light enough to stay in place during the second reflow, or are glued
items.hint: Check heavy inductors, connectors and large ICs on the first-reflowed side with the assembler.

items.text: Parts rated for only one reflow cycle are placed on the second-reflowed side
items.hint: Some connectors, LEDs and sensors only allow a single reflow; check datasheets.

items.text: Every through-hole part has a defined soldering process
items.hint: Wave, selective, pin-in-paste or hand solder. Each has its own pad and keep-out requirements.

items.text: Bottom-side keep-outs around through-hole pins suit selective or wave soldering
items.hint: Selective nozzles need clearance from nearby SMD parts per assembler capability.

items.text: Through-hole drill sizes give suitable clearance over the lead diameter
items.hint: Too tight and leads won't insert; too loose and the barrel doesn't fill. Clearance is a rule of thumb; check with the assembler.

items.text: Through-hole pins connected to planes have thermal relief for barrel fill
items.hint: Solid plane connections sink heat and leave unfilled barrels, especially on thick or heavy-copper boards.

items.text: Parts that can't be washed (open microphones, buzzers, MEMS sensors, unsealed switches) are identified
items.hint: If a wash step is used, these parts must be fitted after washing or protected.

items.text: BGA underfill or corner staking is decided for shock and vibration
items.hint: Underfill hampers rework; decide deliberately and note it on the assembly drawing.

items.text: Assembly drawing (top and bottom views) is current and matches the PCB revision
items.hint: Regenerate it from the release PCB file; old drawings with the right title block are a common trap.

items.text: All DNP components are clearly marked on the assembly drawing
items.hint: Show them hatched or listed per variant so an operator can see what to leave off.

items.text: Special assembly notes are included (solder type, underfill, torque values)
items.hint: Put the notes on the drawing itself, not just in an email to the assembler.

items.text: Conformal coating requirements are specified where applicable
items.hint: Say whether the board is coated, which material, and which areas are masked.

items.text: Press-fit and hand-solder-only components are clearly identified
items.hint: These need separate process steps; the assembler must plan them up front.

items.text: The assembly drawing shows a readable reference designator for every part
items.hint: Check at print scale. Dense areas may need a magnified detail view.

items.text: The board revision and assembly part number appear in the drawing title block
items.hint: The assembly number identifies the variant; the PCB revision identifies the bare board.

items.text: Programming and test steps are called out or a work instruction is referenced
items.hint: Include firmware file names and versions, or point to the controlled document that has them.

items.text: Any rework wires or modifications are documented with routing and fixing method
items.hint: Undocumented bodges are lost on the next build. Give a drawing per mod, with wire type and glue points.

items.text: The cleaning requirement is specified: no-clean residue allowed, or wash required
items.hint: Residue matters for coating adhesion, high-impedance circuits and RF.

items.text: Label, serial number and marking locations are specified
items.hint: Keep labels off vents, heat sources and areas that get coated.

items.text: The coating material type is chosen for the environment and recorded
items.hint: Acrylic, silicone, urethane or parylene differ in moisture, chemical and temperature resistance and in reworkability.

items.text: Coating keep-out areas are defined and masked
items.hint: Connectors, test points, switches, sensor openings, heatsink interfaces and grounding contacts usually stay uncoated.

items.text: Components are compatible with coating
items.hint: Vented sensors, relays, trimmers, unsealed switches and some connectors are damaged or disabled by coating.

items.text: The board is cleaned before coating to a level compatible with the coating
items.hint: Flux residue under coating causes poor adhesion and can lead to corrosion or leakage.

items.text: Potting compound stress and cure heat are checked against the components
items.hint: Hard compounds can crack glass diodes and large ceramic capacitors through shrinkage or CTE mismatch.

items.text: Tall or heavy parts are staked or adhesive-bonded for vibration
items.hint: Electrolytics, inductors and large connectors fatigue their joints under vibration.

items.text: Electrical testing is planned before coating or potting, or test access is kept
items.hint: After potting, faults can't be diagnosed or reworked.

items.text: Press-fit footprints use the connector manufacturer's finished hole size
items.hint: Press-fit needs a tighter tolerance than ordinary plated holes; make sure the fab drawing calls it out.

items.text: Press-fit areas keep components out of the press tool and support keep-outs
items.hint: Check the connector application spec for top and bottom keep-out zones.

items.text: The surface finish is compatible with the press-fit pins
items.hint: Connector datasheets list approved finishes; some pins aren't qualified on every finish.

items.text: Fastener holes have keep-outs for screw heads, washers and tools
items.hint: Check both sides of the board and the driver access path.

items.text: Heatsink attachment, thermal interface material and clamping are specified
items.hint: Name the TIM, its thickness and the fastener torque or clip part number.

items.text: Board-to-board connector stack height and mating tolerance are checked
items.hint: Add up connector heights, standoffs and tolerances against the datasheet's allowed mating range.

items.text: Heavy or cable-loaded connectors have mechanical strain relief
items.hint: Through-hole anchors, screws or brackets stop cable loads from reaching solder joints.

items.text: AOI is planned and part markings and polarity indicators are visible to it
items.hint: Ask the assembler whether AOI runs on every build and what it needs.

items.text: X-ray inspection is specified for BGAs and bottom-terminated components
items.hint: Hidden joints can't be checked optically.

items.text: Void acceptance criteria for thermal pads and BGA balls are agreed
items.hint: Reference IPC-A-610 or state a customer requirement; thermal pads may need a tighter limit for heat flow.

items.text: First-article inspection is requested for the first build
items.hint: FAI catches rotation, polarity and wrong-part errors before the full batch is built.

items.text: Test points are reachable after assembly for flying probe or ICT
items.hint: Check that tall parts, shields and connectors don't block probe access.

items.text: A functional test procedure or fixture is defined for production
items.hint: Say what is tested, with which firmware, and what counts as a pass.

items.text: Traceability is defined: serial number or lot recorded for each board
items.hint: Link the serial number to the BOM revision, firmware version and test result.

items.text: All components meet RoHS / REACH requirements, or exceptions are documented
items.hint: Check each MPN's compliance status, including mechanical items and cables.

items.text: Moisture sensitivity level (MSL) is noted for applicable packages
items.hint: Record MSL in the BOM so the assembler can plan storage and baking.

items.text: ESD-sensitive components are identified and handling requirements noted
items.hint: Especially important for RF front ends, unprotected MOSFET gates and lasers.

items.text: The IPC-A-610 acceptability class is specified for inspection
items.hint: Class 2 for most products; Class 3 for high-reliability.

items.text: The IPC-A-610 assembly class matches the IPC-6012 class on the fab drawing
items.hint: A Class 3 assembly on a Class 2 bare board, or vice versa, is usually a mistake.

items.text: Material declarations (RoHS, REACH SVHC) are collected for the compliance file
items.hint: Distributor and manufacturer sites usually provide them per MPN.

items.text: The assembler holds the certification the product needs
items.hint: For example ISO 13485 for medical or IATF 16949 for automotive.

items.text: All parts are bought from authorized distributors or with documented traceability
items.hint: Broker parts carry counterfeit risk; record and approve any exceptions.

items.text: The BOM is costed at the target volume, with price breaks and MOQs
items.hint: Include reel minimums and assembler attrition allowance.

items.text: Parts are placed on one side where the design allows
items.hint: A single reflow pass saves a stencil, a setup and a process step.

items.text: Through-hole parts are minimized or grouped for one soldering process
items.hint: Each manual or selective solder step adds cost per board.

items.text: Passive values and packages are consolidated to reduce unique BOM lines
items.hint: Fewer feeders and lines cut setup cost and inventory.

items.text: Very small packages (0201, 01005) are used only where needed
items.hint: They raise assembly cost and limit which assemblers can build the board.

items.text: Assembler NRE (stencils, programs, fixtures) is quoted and accepted
items.hint: Include test fixture and programming fixture costs.
